main_text.p: 2 Vitam omnium.)Unum dogma eorum recenset Augustinus, quòd astris imprimis autem septem planetis vitam actionésque hominum & eventa rerum tribuerent. Quod commetum ex nimio astrologiæ iudiciariæ studio profectum est, quem errorem secuti sunt postea Priscillianistæ. 2 Error. Deum unum & eūdem in persona una & ὑπόστασις[?] diuersis nominibus appellari, & diuersas personas ceseri, Patrem cum cogitat: Veritatem cum patefactus est, & Hominem in his terris. Itaque Deum ipsum appellat hominem & naturarum confusionem inducit. 3 Christum ex xxx, AEonibus tanquam flosculum compactum & decerptum esse tanquam Hesiodi Pandoram, unde appellari ἀλ-κυτὸν[?], quòd πᾶν πληρωμα νοσικὸς[?]. 4 Iesum à Christo tanquam duas separatásque personas diuellit. Hinc Nestoriani.
main_text.head: CAP. XVI.
Heracleonitæ unde dicti. Quorum erroris tres hypotheses hic traduntur.
main_text.p: Eracleonitæ ab Heracleone{1} discipulo su-periorum. Duo asserunt{2} principia, unum ex altero, & ex his duobus alia plurima. Feruntur autem suos moriẽtes novo modo quasi redimere, id est, per oleum, balsamum, & aquā, & innocationes, quas Hebraicis verbis dicunt super capita eorum.

page.notes: Running head reads "Cap.16. · AVGVSTINVS"; the chapter number is not a page number, so no page_number is given. Reading "AVGVSTINVS" as AUGUSTINUS per u/v rule. "commetum" is printed as is (probably commentum). The Greek after "appellari" and "quòd" is only partly legible and is marked [?]. The marks {1} and {2} are reference marks in the text; their notes are not on this page. The bottom line "1 Heracl" was read as a catchword "Heracl" with signature "1"; it could also be a footnote beginning, which is uncertain. The woodcut initial E is joined to "racleonitæ" as "Eracleonitæ".
